speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history suggestive of bone fragility. To begin our evaluation, could you tell me your specific age and when you first noticed these physical differences?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency).

Thank you for those details; the combination of virilization at birth (clitoromegaly, labial fusion), early signs of androgen excess in the mother, delayed menarche, and bone fragility is highly characteristic of this condition. Given the history of fractures, I need to assess bone density immediately. REQUEST TEST: Bone_Density_Scan (DEXA) and REQUEST TEST: 17-Hydroxyprogesterone level.
